web/plugin_policy/availability.py:R6:_Bo: R6 `except (SecretsError, SecretNotFoundError): return None` in `_BoundSecretInventory.server_generation`. The value is Tier-3: whatever the server secret backend returns for an operator-held credential ref. The method's declared contract is `str | None`, where `None` means "this principal cannot be shown a provable credential generation right now" - it is a stated outcome, not an absence of one. The handler is reachable only after the `self._server_store.has_secret(name)` guard on the line above has already said the ref exists, so the two admitted exception types cover exactly the two ways that can stop being true between the presence check and the read: the ref was removed (SecretNotFoundError) or the backend/decryption could not produce it (SecretsError). What the swallow protects is the generation token that binds one `ProfileAvailability` to the exact credential material behind it: `_LLMProfileResolver.profile_availability` turns a `None` generation into `ProfileAvailability(usable=False, reason=ProfileUnavailableReason.CREDENTIAL_MISSING)` with `generation=None`, and `build_plugin_snapshot` then drops that alias from `usable_profile_aliases`, records `PluginAvailability(plugin_id, PluginUnavailableReason.PROFILE_UNAVAILABLE)` and never adds the plugin to `available`. The swallow's only reachable outcome is therefore a CLOSED availability decision - the profile becomes unselectable - and never a usable profile carrying a fabricated or stale generation. `_binding_fingerprint` only ever sees generations of profiles that stayed usable, so a swallowed fault cannot silently alter a fingerprint a later request would compare against. Narrowing the handler to `SecretNotFoundError` alone would not clear this rule (it stays R6 at the same line) and would let a transient backend fault raise out of an availability listing whose every other outcome is a recorded, operator-repairable `PluginUnavailableReason`.
